note_claims.claim: The patient is presenting with worsening exertional breathlessness and COPD.
The patient has a history of MRC dyspnoea grade 3.
The patient has a history of morning cough with white sputum.
The patient has had two exacerbations requiring oral steroids in the last 12 months, one of which also required antibiotics.
The patient has no history of hospital admissions.
The patient reports ankle swelling.
The patient has no history of chest pain, haemoptysis, or weight loss.
The patient is an ex-smoker for 6 months, with an approximate pack-year history of 40.
The patient has received flu and pneumococcal vaccines.
The patient is prescribed Anoro Ellipta (umeclidinium/vilanterol) once daily.
The patient is prescribed Salmeterol as needed (about twice daily).
The patient's oxygen level is 93 percent on air.
The patient's breathing rate is 20.
There is bilateral wheeze noted.
There are coarse crackles at the bottom of the left lung, at the left base (new finding).
Spirometry shows an FEV1 of 52 percent of predicted, which is lower than last year.
The patient's blood eosinophil count last month was 0.35 × 10⁹/L.
The patient has COPD with frequent exacerbations despite LAMA/LABA.
The patient's eosinophil count (0.35) is suitable for triple therapy.
There are new focal crackles at the left base.
The plan is to switch the patient from Anoro to Trelegy Ellipta, one puff once daily.
The patient is referred to pulmonary rehabilitation.
A chest X-ray is ordered today due to crackles at the left base.
The patient is scheduled for a clinic review in three months.
The patient should contact their GP the same day if there is increased breathlessness, sputum volume, or a change in sputum colour.
The patient should call 999 if they are very breathless.

transcript_facts.fact: Clinician is Dr Nwosu from the respiratory team.
Patient identifies his wife as Valerie.
Patient reports worsening breathlessness and needs to stop halfway up the hill to the shops.
Patient can walk on the flat at his own pace but is slower than Valerie.
Patient has a cough most mornings with white phlegm.
Patient has had two flare-ups in the last year (one in January, one in summer).
Both flare-ups required prednisolone, and the summer one also needed antibiotics.
Patient has no hospital admissions.
Patient reports no swelling in his ankles.
Relative clarifies that the swollen ankles belong to her, not the patient's.
Patient reports no chest pain or coughing up blood.
Patient reports no weight loss, stating he has been steady.
Patient stopped smoking six months ago and has not smoked since.
Patient smoked twenty cigarettes a day for forty years, stopping for ten years in the middle, resulting in thirty years of smoking.
Patient is using Anoro once a day and the blue inhaler maybe twice a day.
Patient has had both the flu jab and the pneumonia jab at the surgery.
Patient has no known drug allergies, only the inhalers.
Examination findings include SpO2 of 93% on air and a breathing rate of 20.
Examination findings include wheeze on both sides and coarse crackles at the bottom of the left lung, at the left base.
Spirometry shows an FEV1 of 52 percent of predicted, which is lower than last year.
Patient's blood eosinophil count last month was 0.35.
Clinician recommends adding a steroid to the inhalers because the patient is still having flare-ups.
Clinician proposes switching the Anoro to Trelegy, one puff once a day, which includes the same two medicines plus an inhaled steroid.
Clinician recommends referring the patient to pulmonary rehabilitation.
Clinician orders a chest X-ray today because of the crackles at the left base.
The patient is scheduled for a clinic review in three months.
Safety netting advice: Contact GP the same day if there is increased breathlessness, sputum volume, or a change in sputum colour.
Safety netting advice: Call 999 if the patient is very breathless.
